stem: Which discharge-teaching approach best reflects AHRQ's IDEAL Discharge Planning strategy?

options.A: Provide education throughout the hospital stay and assess understanding with teach-back rather than waiting until the moment of discharge.
options.B: Give all instructions only after the client has left the facility.
options.C: Avoid checking comprehension because repeating information can confuse clients.
options.D: Limit discharge education to a printed medication list without discussion.

rationale: AHRQ IDEAL Discharge Planning emphasizes educating the patient and family throughout the stay, using clear explanations, and assessing understanding with teach-back.
educational_objective: Use ongoing education and teach-back as part of safe discharge planning.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_locator: IDEAL strategy — Educate throughout the hospital stay; Assess how well doctors and nurses explain; use teach-back
source_claim_supported: Discharge education should occur throughout the stay and understanding should be assessed using techniques such as teach-back.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9/PDF p.13
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — discharge education
correction_summary: Reclassified the item from Basic Care and Comfort to Health Promotion and Maintenance and anchored it to AHRQ's ongoing education/teach-back approach.
